title: AI for Admin: Inbox, Scheduling & Meeting Notes
summary: A human-reviewed workflow for triaging inboxes, drafting replies, converting meeting notes into actions, summarizing documents, and preparing routine forms.
audience: Administrative professionals, executive assistants, founders, and operations teams.
learningPaths: Verify names, dates, commitments, and permissions
evidence: Authoritative calendar, email, and meeting records
assumptions: A responsible human retains account control
Sensitive data stays in approved systems
limitations: AI can misread tone, commitments, dates, and recipients
External messages and account changes require human approval

title: AI for Client Service
summary: Use AI to draft client updates, meeting recaps, project-status summaries, and onboarding communications while keeping a human accountable for every message.
audience: Account managers, consultants, agencies, and small service teams.
learningPaths: Gather approved client and project facts
Check scope, tone, dates, and promises
Send and preserve the final version
methodology: Ground drafts in the client record
assumptions: The sender has authority to communicate
A human reviews every client-facing output
limitations: AI can invent status, commitments, or context
Professional duties and contractual requirements still apply

title: AI for Governance
summary: Build a clear AI-use policy, data tiers, review gates, disclosure rules, exception handling, and an evidence trail so teams can adopt AI responsibly.
audience: Leaders, operators, legal teams, and governance owners formalizing organizational AI use.
learningPaths: Review policy performance on a cadence
assumptions: Leadership supports enforcement
Qualified experts review jurisdiction-specific requirements
limitations: This educational resource is not legal advice
Governance requires continuing oversight, training, and maintenance

title: AI for Knowledge Management
summary: Turn scattered documents, wikis, and messages into a source-grounded answer system with ownership, citations, permissions, freshness controls, and review.
audience: Teams whose operational knowledge is fragmented or difficult to retrieve.
assumptions: Owners can identify authoritative versions
Access rules are technically enforceable
limitations: Retrieval cannot repair missing or contradictory knowledge
Permissions and freshness require maintenance

title: AI for Law Firms
summary: A safety-first legal workflow for accelerating research, drafting, review, and knowledge work while verifying authority and keeping licensed attorneys accountable.
audience: Law firms and legal teams evaluating supervised AI-assisted work.
learningPaths: Classify the task and governing duties
Draft with source links and uncertainty
evidence: Attorney review and final work product
assumptions: Licensed attorneys remain responsible
The firm has approved data and tool controls
limitations: This resource is education, not legal advice
AI cannot determine competence, strategy, or the law without accountable lawyers

title: AI for Leadership
summary: Use AI to compress information, surface assumptions, prepare pre-mortems, compare options, and improve communication while reserving accountable decisions for leaders.
audience: Founders, executives, directors, and team leads managing complex information and decisions.
learningPaths: Make and document the human decision
methodology: Use AI to widen and compress
assumptions: Leaders can identify authoritative evidence
AI supports rather than makes consequential decisions
limitations: Models can reinforce framing bias or invent certainty
Leadership judgment and stakeholder responsibility cannot be delegated

title: AI for Marketing
summary: A practical workflow for drafting, repurposing, briefing, and channel adaptation while a human editor protects voice, facts, claims, permissions, and strategy.
audience: Small-business marketers, creators, founders, agencies, and communications teams.
evidence: Final human edits and performance data
assumptions: A human owns strategy and publication
Source rights and disclosure requirements are resolved
limitations: AI can homogenize voice and fabricate claims
Generation does not replace strategy, legal review, or editorial judgment

title: AI for Operations: Turn Tribal Knowledge into SOPs
summary: Use AI to capture and draft SOPs, checklists, runbooks, and status summaries while process owners verify every step before it becomes canonical.
audience: Owners, operators, managers, and teams documenting repeatable work.
learningPaths: Map triggers, steps, branches, and exceptions
methodology: Version and maintain the approved procedure
assumptions: A knowledgeable owner validates the process
The procedure can be tested safely
limitations: AI cannot recover undisclosed steps
Consequential procedures require qualified review

title: AI for Research
summary: Use AI for market scans, document synthesis, interview analysis, and knowledge bases while preserving citations, search boundaries, verification, and human ownership of conclusions.
audience: Researchers, analysts, consultants, students, and evidence-oriented teams.
learningPaths: Define the question and evidence standard
Use AI for discovery or extraction
assumptions: Researchers can access authoritative sources
Qualified humans own consequential interpretations
limitations: AI search and synthesis can omit or distort evidence
Coverage depends on sources, access, tools, and date

title: AI for Sales
summary: A human-approved workflow for call preparation, discovery-note synthesis, follow-up drafts, proposal first drafts, and CRM hygiene—not autonomous outbound spam.
audience: Consultants, agencies, founders, and small sales teams.
learningPaths: Define fit and legitimate source boundaries
Approve communications and update the CRM
methodology: Require human approval and lawful outreach
assumptions: The organization has authority to contact prospects
A human owns every external message
limitations: This resource does not establish compliance with outreach law
Enrichment and generated personalization may be stale or inappropriate

title: AI for Small Businesses
summary: Practical, bounded AI workflows for email, marketing, product copy, customer answers, knowledge, and operations without pretending automation replaces business ownership.
audience: Small-business owners, founders, and lean teams beginning responsible AI adoption.
learningPaths: Choose one expensive or repetitive workflow
Measure time, quality, risk, and cost
Document and expand only from evidence
methodology: Measure failure as well as speed
assumptions: The business can name an accountable owner
Consequential work remains human-approved
limitations: AI is not a substitute for staffing, strategy, or professional expertise
Tool benefits depend on process and data quality

title: AI for Training
summary: Turn approved SOPs and expert knowledge into training modules, scenarios, role-plays, quizzes, and coaching aids with mandatory expert review.
audience: Managers, educators, learning teams, and subject-matter experts building workplace training.
learningPaths: Have experts verify accuracy and fairness
assumptions: Subject-matter experts validate content
Learner data is handled appropriately
limitations: AI can teach errors from incomplete sources
Generated assessments may be biased, ambiguous, or poor measures of competence
